purpose: Requirements for advancing the failover chain on Anthropic account-level refusals.

requirements.statement: classify as an account-level refusal a response from an upstream the Anthropic adapter serves directly or through a Claude OAuth pool (a Kimi OAuth pool is out of scope and relays these unchanged) with HTTP 400 whose error message starts with `You have reached your specified API usage limits` or `You have reached your specified workspace API usage limits` (a spend limit the account owner set)

scenarios.name: When the first upstream of a two-element chain answers 400 `invalid_request_error` with `You have reached your specified API usage limits. You will regain access on 2026-11-01 at 00:00 UTC.`, the system shall send the request to the second upstream and return its response.
when: the first upstream of a two-element chain answers 400 `invalid_request_error` with `You have reached your specified API usage limits. You will regain access on 2026-11-01 at 00:00 UTC.`
then: send the request to the second upstream and return its response

scenarios.name: When an upstream answers 400 with `You have reached your specified workspace API usage limits`, the system shall classify it as an account-level refusal.
when: an upstream answers 400 with `You have reached your specified workspace API usage limits`
then: classify it as an account-level refusal

requirements.statement: classify as an account-level refusal a response from an upstream the Anthropic adapter serves directly or through a Claude OAuth pool (a Kimi OAuth pool is out of scope and relays these unchanged) with HTTP 400 or 402 whose error message starts with `Your credit balance is too low to access the Anthropic API` (prepaid or plan-included credit exhausted)

scenarios.name: When an upstream answers 400 with `Your credit balance is too low to access the Anthropic API. Please go to Plans & Billing to upgrade or purchase credits.`, the system shall advance to the next chain element.
when: an upstream answers 400 with `Your credit balance is too low to access the Anthropic API. Please go to Plans & Billing to upgrade or purchase credits.`
then: advance to the next chain element

scenarios.name: When an upstream answers 402 `billing_error` with the credit-balance message, the system shall classify it as an account-level refusal.
when: an upstream answers 402 `billing_error` with the credit-balance message
then: classify it as an account-level refusal

requirements.statement: classify as an account-level refusal a response from an upstream the Anthropic adapter serves directly or through a Claude OAuth pool (a Kimi OAuth pool is out of scope and relays these unchanged) with HTTP 402 and error type `billing_error`

scenarios.name: When an upstream answers 402 `billing_error` with any other message, the system shall advance to the next chain element.
when: an upstream answers 402 `billing_error` with any other message
then: advance to the next chain element

requirements.statement: advance the failover chain to the next element on an account-level refusal, the same way it advances on a 429, both before response headers are committed to the client and inside an already committed streaming response

scenarios.name: When the first upstream of a two-element chain answers 400 `invalid_request_error` with `You have reached your specified API usage limits. You will regain access on 2026-11-01 at 00:00 UTC.`, the system shall send the request to the second upstream and return its response.
when: the first upstream of a two-element chain answers 400 `invalid_request_error` with `You have reached your specified API usage limits. You will regain access on 2026-11-01 at 00:00 UTC.`
then: send the request to the second upstream and return its response

scenarios.name: When an upstream answers 400 with `Your credit balance is too low to access the Anthropic API. Please go to Plans & Billing to upgrade or purchase credits.`, the system shall advance to the next chain element.
when: an upstream answers 400 with `Your credit balance is too low to access the Anthropic API. Please go to Plans & Billing to upgrade or purchase credits.`
then: advance to the next chain element

scenarios.name: When an upstream answers 402 `billing_error` with any other message, the system shall advance to the next chain element.
when: an upstream answers 402 `billing_error` with any other message
then: advance to the next chain element

scenarios.name: When a committed streaming response's current chain element answers with an account-level refusal, the system shall continue the stream from the next chain element instead of emitting a terminal error event.
when: a committed streaming response's current chain element answers with an account-level refusal
then: continue the stream from the next chain element instead of emitting a terminal error event

requirements.statement: keep every other 400 and 402 response terminal: relay it to the client unchanged after the bounded body inspection, without trying another upstream

scenarios.name: If an upstream answers 400 `invalid_request_error` with a request-validation message such as `messages: Field required`, then the system shall return that 400 to the client without contacting any later chain element.
when: an upstream answers 400 `invalid_request_error` with a request-validation message such as `messages: Field required`
then: return that 400 to the client without contacting any later chain element

scenarios.name: If an upstream answers 400 with a message that contains `usage limits` but does not start with one of the FR-1 phrases, then the system shall treat it as terminal.
when: an upstream answers 400 with a message that contains `usage limits` but does not start with one of the FR-1 phrases
then: treat it as terminal

requirements.statement: skip a credential the gateway owns (an API-key upstream, or one account of a Claude subscription pool) for new requests after it returns an account-level refusal, until the refusal's stated access-resume time for a spend-limit refusal, or for 1 hour for a refusal that states no time

scenarios.name: While an API-key upstream is within the skip window set by a spend-limit refusal that stated `2026-11-01 at 00:00 UTC`, the system shall route new requests past it without contacting it.
given: an API-key upstream is within the skip window set by a spend-limit refusal that stated `2026-11-01 at 00:00 UTC`
then: route new requests past it without contacting it

scenarios.name: When the stated access-resume time has passed, the system shall send the next request to that upstream again.
when: the stated access-resume time has passed
then: send the next request to that upstream again

scenarios.name: When an upstream returns a credit-balance or `billing_error` refusal, the system shall skip it for 1 hour.
when: an upstream returns a credit-balance or `billing_error` refusal
then: skip it for 1 hour

scenarios.name: If a spend-limit refusal's access-resume time cannot be read, then the system shall skip the upstream for 1 hour.
when: a spend-limit refusal's access-resume time cannot be read
then: skip the upstream for 1 hour

requirements.statement: rotate a Claude subscription pool to its next account on an account-level refusal before the chain moves to the next upstream, consistent with how the pool already handles account-scoped failures

scenarios.name: When one account of a Claude subscription pool returns an account-level refusal, the system shall try the pool's next eligible account before advancing to the next upstream.
when: one account of a Claude subscription pool returns an account-level refusal
then: try the pool's next eligible account before advancing to the next upstream

requirements.statement: never put a client-supplied credential (passthrough authentication) into the skip state, because the refusal belongs to that client's key and not to the upstream

scenarios.name: When a passthrough-authenticated upstream returns an account-level refusal, the system shall advance the chain for that request and shall not skip the upstream for later requests.
when: a passthrough-authenticated upstream returns an account-level refusal
then: advance the chain for that request and shall not skip the upstream for later requests

requirements.statement: hold the skip state in memory only; a restart clears it

scenarios.name: When the gateway restarts, the system shall treat every previously skipped credential as eligible.
then: treat every previously skipped credential as eligible

requirements.statement: when the chain is exhausted with no successful response and an account-level refusal was the best remembered failure, return it to the client with the upstream's own status and error message intact, under the existing preference order

scenarios.name: When the only chain element returns a spend-limit refusal, the system shall return HTTP 400 with the upstream's original message.
when: the only chain element returns a spend-limit refusal
then: return HTTP 400 with the upstream's original message

requirements.statement: update the failover contract and the user-facing failover and troubleshooting documentation, including every maintained translation, to describe the three refusals, the skip durations, and that all other 400s stay terminal
try a chain whose every element is in the skip window as configured instead of refusing locally, so a credential that was topped up or raised is noticed before its window ends

scenarios.name: While every element of a chain is in the skip window, the system shall send the request to the chain's elements in their configured order.
given: every element of a chain is in the skip window
then: send the request to the chain's elements in their configured order

requirements.statement: read an error body for refusal classification only for 400 and 402 responses, within a fixed budget, so other statuses decide failover from the status line alone (except where a path already buffers bodies for another reason, such as alias routes)
leave successful and non-refusal responses byte-for-byte unchanged, including streaming responses

log each account-level refusal at warning level with the upstream name and the refusal kind, log the skip expiry only for a credential that is actually skipped (not for passthrough), log the account cooldown for a Claude pool refusal, and count the advance in the existing failover metric
